headline: High data-leakage and compliance risk: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer-data handling can expose sensitive support data when paired with the docs-only ai-engineering-hub.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it is not a strong injection source. B has API integrations and handles messages, but there is no documented shared channel or default parsing path between them. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer or an undocumented workspace, so the pathway is weak and not default.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies B-generated text into A as instructions
IF an undocumented shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced between A and B
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted support content into A
Add a human review step before any A-side instruction execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress plus third-party integrations. A is docs-only and not shown to be local-only or isolated from B’s workspace, so if any shared workspace or handoff exists, sensitive support data can leak outward through B’s integrations. Uncertainty about A’s isolation pushes this to high.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem, clipboard, or exported transcript
IF B forwards conversation content into Slack, Shopify, Linear, or Dialogflow integrations
mitigations: Restrict B integrations to non-sensitive channels
Separate A and B workspaces and credentials
Redact customer identifiers before any handoff
Review outbound integration logs for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write surfaces and no network egress, while B’s documented integrations are outbound APIs rather than shared mutable storage. There is no evidence of overlapping write access to the same directory, git state, or database, so direct capability conflict is limited. If an undocumented shared mutable resource exists, severity would rise, but that is not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same shared directory or repository
IF an external orchestrator grants both write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate storage locations
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use file locks or single-writer scheduling
Check integration scopes before enabling them

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume messages and reports, and its integrations suggest it may act on upstream content. A is docs-only and could produce unverified guidance or generated text that B might relay or operationalize. Because there is no documented verification boundary between them, A’s output could cascade into B’s customer-facing actions, though the exact automation path is not proven.
conditions: IF A-generated text is imported into B as a source of truth
IF B forwards A-derived content to customers or internal tools without review
mitigations: Require human approval before B sends A-derived content
Label A output as unverified in B
Add source citations to any imported A content
Sample-check outbound messages for hallucinations
requires-engineering: add verification gates between A and B

E_compliance.rationale: B clearly handles customer data and related records, while A is an open-source docs-only asset with no stated privacy controls, retention policy, or residency guarantees. If customer data from B is routed into A’s environment or documentation workflow, compliance gaps can arise immediately. Because A’s controls are unspecified, uncertainty escalates the risk rather than lowering it.
conditions: IF B customer records are exported into A’s environment
IF A is used to process regulated customer data without a documented DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A
Document retention and deletion rules for B exports
Confirm residency and DPA coverage before any transfer
Minimize fields in any shared export
requires-engineering: implement compliance controls and audit logging
